key_insight: In medical foundation models, representational convergence is driven more by the self-supervised pretraining objective than by clinical supervision or model scale.
clinical_relevance: A linear classifier can transfer across encoders and to external hospitals, but the shared geometry is still imperfect and weaker where clinical judgment matters most.
method: Compared 18 image and 7 text encoders across 5 imaging modalities
Controlled experiments varied only the training objective while keeping data, architecture, and scale fixed
Evaluated similarity, scalability, and transfer across six chest radiography datasets and held-out hospitals
evidence_signal: Across 650,982 chest radiographs, matched self-supervised encoders aligned most (40.4%), outperforming label-supervised (21.1%) and image-text (3.3%) models.
watch_item: The observed convergence is modest, within-modality, and does not match radiologists' similarity judgments, so interoperability may fail in underrepresented subgroups or edge cases.
paper_title: Self-supervision drives representational convergence in medical foundation models more than clinical supervision
